la-conservation-district-supervisors.concept: Soil and water conservation district board
la-conservation-district-supervisors.area: Louisiana — all 44 soil and water conservation districts
la-conservation-district-supervisors.summary: The Parish card lists the soil and water conservation district that covers your parish, with its offices and telephones. It names none of the district's five supervisors, and where two districts share a parish it lists both.
la-conservation-district-supervisors.why: Three supervisors are elected and two are appointed by the state's Soil and Water Conservation Commission. The state's list of district offices names none of them, and neither does the Secretary of State's list of elected officials.
la-conservation-district-supervisors.wanted: A list of each district's five current supervisors from the Department of Agriculture and Forestry, and a map file of the districts' lines, so that the seven parishes divided between two districts can be drawn.

la-court-election-sections.area: Louisiana — the judicial and court of appeal districts divided into election sections
la-court-election-sections.summary: In some Louisiana judicial districts and court of appeal districts each judge is elected from one part of the district. This app does not draw those parts, so the card names every judge of the district and the part each is elected from.
la-court-election-sections.why: State law sets many of those parts by voting precinct. The court of appeal card can say which part a whole parish is in; the district court card cannot say which part you are in.
la-court-election-sections.wanted: Maps of the election sections of Louisiana's judicial and court of appeal districts, or each section's current list of voting precincts.

la-municipal-ward-lines.area: Louisiana — its cities, towns and villages other than Lafayette, Bossier City, Central and Slidell
la-municipal-ward-lines.summary: The City, Town or Village card names the council. Where members are elected by ward or district it cannot say which one represents the spot you picked; in Lafayette, Bossier City, Central and Slidell the City Council District card does.
la-municipal-ward-lines.why: The Census Bureau maps no town's wards or districts, so they come only from a city's own current map. Some large cities' maps are out of date, unconfirmed, only a PDF or not free to copy, and in most towns the list names no ward.
la-municipal-ward-lines.wanted: Each other city's and town's current ward or council district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines this project may copy, and, where the list names no ward, a town page or ordinance saying how its members are elected.

la-parish-district-lines.area: Louisiana — the parishes whose current police jury or council district lines are not confirmed
la-parish-district-lines.summary: In 56 of Louisiana's 64 parishes this app names the members of the police jury or council but cannot show which one represents the spot you picked, because it has no confirmed map of the current district lines there.
la-parish-district-lines.why: The Census Bureau's map still carries older lines in most parishes, and no statewide map of the current ones has been found. Old lines would name the wrong member for many people.
la-parish-district-lines.wanted: Each parish's current district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines, or one statewide map of every parish's current lines from a state office.

la-school-board-district-lines.summary: The School District card names every member of the school board, and it cannot say which one represents the spot you picked, because this app has no map of the boards' election districts.
la-school-board-district-lines.why: Nearly every member is elected from a district the Secretary of State's list names, and the Census Bureau does not map school board election districts. No statewide map of them has been found.
la-school-board-district-lines.wanted: Each school board's current election district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines, or one statewide map of every board's districts from a state office.

la-tribal-government.area: The Coushatta Tribe's land, in Allen, Natchitoches, Calcasieu and Jefferson Davis parishes
la-tribal-government.summary: The Tribal Government card names the councils of three of Louisiana's four nations, the Chitimacha, the Jena Band of Choctaw and the Tunica-Biloxi, from each nation's own page. It names nobody for the Coushatta Tribe.
la-tribal-government.why: The Coushatta Tribe's own site names its chairman and says the council has five members without naming the other four, and part of a council is not shown as if it were all of it.
la-tribal-government.wanted: A list of the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana's whole council, from the tribe, that this project may read.
